candidates.targetedCausalLink: Concurrent requests with one exact organization/pipeline cache key independently execute the same full ordered application-table read after a miss.
candidates.expectedCapacityEffect: One application full-table read owner per exact process-local cache key and overlapping miss window; all same-key waiters share the owner result.
candidates.userLatencyEffect: Removes duplicate owner contention for overlapping same-key misses without extending the 30-second result TTL.
dependencies: Keep in-flight ownership distinct from result-cache TTL
unknownAssumptions: Accepted P09 exact route admission count is not observable
Benefit across multiple service instances is not provided
evidenceSupporting: Phase 2.2C statically proves no in-flight owner
Accepted P09 cause explicitly includes CONCURRENT and UNCOALESCED full-table reads
P09 synchronized same component-list requests use one organization/pipeline read key
counterevidence: The owner still performs one full-table read
Process-local ownership cannot eliminate cross-instance duplicate reads
candidates.decisionReason: Smallest independently testable intervention that directly removes the diagnosed duplicate read count without changing query or response semantics.

candidates.targetedCausalLink: Each owner reads and maps the full organization/pipeline table before applying business-safe component search in memory.
candidates.expectedCapacityEffect: Reduce rows and columns returned and owner-side mapping cost, but retain one query per concurrent miss unless paired with C01.
candidates.userLatencyEffect: Potentially faster owner query, subject to equivalent predicates and index support.
dependencies: Business-safe fallback fields must be queryable or equivalently reconstructed
Case, null, locale, deleted-row, tenant, and ordering semantics must match
unknownAssumptions: Expected result cardinality reduction is not measured
JSON-carried description search cannot be represented by the current top-level predicate
evidenceSupporting: Current P09 read returns all matching organization/pipeline rows and all model columns
Filtering and grouping happen after business-safe JSON fallback mapping
counterevidence: Existing indexes do not cover componentName/componentCode search
Current q semantics include descriptionPl/descriptionEn recovered from JSON carriers
candidates.decisionReason: Complementary read-cost reduction, but not the smallest first experiment and carries materially larger semantic and index uncertainty.
candidates.conditionalTrigger: IF C01 proves one owner read per exact miss window but P09 remains capacity-bound or the single owner read remains materially costly, THEN evaluate C02 with semantic-equivalence and index-plan gates.

candidates.targetedCausalLink: Client timeout ends waiting while admitted server and database work continues.
candidates.expectedCapacityEffect: Reduce retained work after clients leave; does not prevent the synchronized duplicate reads that begin before timeout.
candidates.userLatencyEffect: No benefit before timeout; potentially faster recovery after overload.
unknownAssumptions: Prisma query cancellation is not proven
Exact layer retaining P09 work is not separately timed
evidenceSupporting: 766 clients timed out while application DB work remained after cooldown
counterevidence: Cancellation starts after fan-out already exists
No route or Prisma AbortSignal exists today
candidates.decisionReason: Evidence supports damage limitation after timeout, not prevention of the established first cause.
candidates.conditionalTrigger: IF C01 is accepted yet timeout/abort cases still leave material server or DB work, THEN prove driver cancellation feasibility and evaluate C03 separately.

candidates.targetedCausalLink: Bound the number of simultaneous expensive reads admitted to the application/DB path.
candidates.expectedCapacityEffect: Cap simultaneous pressure while preserving redundant work as queued or rejected requests.
candidates.userLatencyEffect: Potential queue delay, head-of-line blocking, starvation, rejection, and tenant fairness effects.
unknownAssumptions: Distinct-key capacity after duplicate removal is unknown
evidenceSupporting: P09 is proven through 100 and blocked at 1000
counterevidence: A cap can merely hide overload behind queue latency
candidates.decisionReason: A concurrency cap is not justified before redundant same-key reads are removed and the remaining distinct-key capacity is measured.
candidates.reconsiderationEvidence: Controlled post-C01 evidence showing overload from simultaneous distinct-key owner reads plus a bounded fairness/tail-latency contract.

candidates.expectedCapacityEffect: Unknown; pool changes could increase throughput or amplify database overload.
candidates.userLatencyEffect: Unknown until acquisition wait is directly observed.
dependencies: Database capacity envelope after query fan-out controls
unknownAssumptions: Prisma acquisition count and wait are NOT_OBSERVABLE
counterevidence: The waiter metric is not the Prisma acquisition queue
No pool error or saturation was proven
candidates.decisionReason: Pool tuning depends on an explicitly unobservable boundary and cannot be promoted from PostgreSQL wait_event evidence.
candidates.reconsiderationEvidence: Direct client-side acquisition count/wait telemetry and isolated database-capacity evidence after C01/C02 evaluation.

candidates.targetedCausalLink: Prevent one stress scenario from contaminating the next scenario measurement.
candidates.expectedCapacityEffect: No production capacity effect; improves test attribution and reproducibility.
dependencies: Fresh process or full settlement gate between scenarios
evidenceSupporting: Clean P10 disproved the shared-process application DB anomaly
counterevidence: Does not alter P09 production reads or capacity
candidates.decisionReason: Retained as mandatory validation hygiene, but rejected as the Phase 2.3 production optimization because it does not address the P09 cause.
